answer: Use a kiosk-verified identity passport. An operator shows a government ID at a kiosk and passes a live face scan in 12 minutes for $35. The kiosk signs one onyx-sealed credential bound to one agent key, so one face cannot mint a second passport. It expires after 90 days unless renewed in person, and flagged passports join a public revocation list. Forging 10,000 agents needs 10,000 visits, $350,000 in fees, and 2,000 travel hours, and a stolen ID fails the scan. Like a harbor checking papers before docking, only verified agents enter paid work, while a nebula of clones stays outside.
